sources.citation: Limbu, Man Kumari (2007). An ethnolinguistic observation of Chhulung Rai, a highly endangered language. 50 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: The language is not in the catalog and no existing statements exist; this work adds nothing on stress. Original URL host (www.socialinclusion.org.np) no longer resolves (attempt 1: DNS failure); archived copy (Internet Archive, 10 Apr 2016) could not be reached by automated download (attempt 2: connect failure); the copy already saved held by the project on 2026-09-17 is the correct item (title, author, 50 pp., page numbering verified) and was re-read in full.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1/5.3 languoid chhu1238; OLAC page for cur (the Internet Archive 2026-06-07); Ethnologue 'Chhiling' cur (the Internet Archive 2024-11-30); Wikipedia 'Chulung language'.
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog lists only the three Limbu items (plus Gerber 2023 pp. 68-69 on subclassification and Campbell et al. 2022 on endangerment); OLAC lists no descriptive resource beyond Glottolog/Ethnologue/LINGUIST List; Ethnologue names Chhiling with no dialects; Wikipedia has no phonology section. Nepalese Linguistics vols 25 and 29 also a full-text search for stress/accent: no Chhulung matter; vols 24 and 30 arrived truncated from the Internet Archive.

sources.citation: Rai, Ichchha Purna. 2013. A contrastive study of Chhintang and English pronouns: problems and teaching strategies. Nepalese Linguistics 28: 155-161. (Same volume: Paudyal, Netra P. 2013. Issues of v-v compounds in Chintang, pp. 125ff.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Chhulung stress. Rai's paper is on Chhintang (uses 'Chhulung' once, p. 159) and its 'no voice and no tone' line is Ethnologue's Chintang note; Paudyal p. 125 names 'Chɨlɨng (also pronounced as Chiling or Chulung)' with Athpare and Belhare as Chintang's nearest relatives.

sources.citation: Limbu, Man Kumari. 2007 [approval letter dated 2064/11/07 BS]. An ethnolinguistic observation of Chhulung Rai, a highly endangered language. Final narrative report to the Social Inclusion Research Fund (SIRF/SNV Nepal), apprenticeship grant SIRF/AG/07, supervised by Madhav P. Pokharel (TU). 50 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2 'Phonology' (pp. 15-26) gives 26 consonant and 6 vowel phonemes with minimal pairs, Devanagari orthography and pronouns; the conclusion list (p. 25) notes 'Vowels length is not phonemic', 'not any diphthongs so far', 'not any dialect so far'. The words stress/accent/tone/pitch/syllable never occur. Original host (socialinclusion.org.np) is dead; downloaded from the Internet Archive copy of 2016-04-10.

sources.note: Not a Chhulung source, but Paudyal (NepLing 28, 2013, p. 125) names Chɨlɨng/Chulung with Athpare and Belhare as Chintang's nearest relatives; a Chintang phonology sketch is the only nearby description that could be used as a stated proxy or that might mention Chhulung.
